# Oracle Database Laboratories

Database Systems coursework from Wrocław University of Science and Technology, republished as a
curated SQL suite. **One toy domain — a herd of cats organised into hunting bands — carries almost the
entire Oracle feature surface.** 15 SQL scripts (96,728 bytes, measured 2026-08-05), 4 issued
assignment sheets as PDFs, a Mermaid-rendered ER diagram, a README and `docs/schema.md`.

> "Five relations are enough to reach most of what Oracle offers — a self-referencing hierarchy, a
> circular foreign key, cursors, packages, compound triggers, and the object-relational layer on top
> of all of it."
> — Oracle-Database-Laboratories/README.md, 2026-07-25

## Stack

[[oracle-database]] 12c or later (XE is enough), driven as [[sql-plus]] `@` scripts, with
[[plsql]] for everything in `03_` and `04_`. The only external build step in the repository is
`mermaid-cli` rendering `docs/schema.md` into `assets/schema-er-diagram.png` — otherwise
[[zero-dependency-no-build-step]] holds exactly.

## The four stages

Directory numbers are a dependency edge, not a table of contents — the local instance of

`01_schema`, so the relational schema must exist first.

| `sql/03_plsql/` | blocks, cursors, packages, triggers | [[plsql-exception-handling]] · [[plsql-cursors]] · [[database-triggers]] |

## The data model

Five relations. `FUNCTIONS` (role → allowed mice-ration band, doubling as a validation table),
`ENEMIES`, `CATS`, `BANDS`, `INCIDENTS` (composite primary key `(nickname, enemy_name)`). Two
structural properties drive every exercise built on top:

- **A self-referencing hierarchy.** `CATS.chief` points back at `CATS.nickname`, `TIGER` is the root,
  the tree is four levels deep. Every `CONNECT BY` in the repo walks it — see [[hierarchical-queries]].
- **A circular foreign key.** `CATS.band_no` → `BANDS.band_no` and `BANDS.band_chief` →
  `CATS.nickname`. Resolved by creating `CATS` without its band key and closing the loop with
  `ALTER TABLE` — see [[circular-fk-via-alter-table]].

The object-relational lab rebuilds the same domain as `cat_type` / `common_type` / `elite_type` /
`account_type` / `incident_type`, and adds three tables (`COMMONS`, `ELITES`, `ACCOUNTS`) with no
relational counterpart.

## Findings

- **The comments are the deliverable.** Nearly every script leads with the trap it is avoiding —
  `ROWNUM` evaluated before `ORDER BY`, `BETWEEN` on a `DATE` silently dropping the last day, a
  PL/SQL parameter shadowing the column it is compared against, `RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR` outside
  `-20000..-20999`. This is the densest instance of [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]] among the
  coursework repos.
- **Superseded work is kept on purpose.** `04_triggers.sql` retains a three-trigger + package-state
  implementation *and* labels it inferior to the compound trigger beside it. That is
  [[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]] used pedagogically rather than archivally — see
  [[compound-trigger-over-package-state]].
- **Essentially no documentation drift.** `README.md`, `docs/schema.md` and the scripts agree on the
  run order, the circular key, the hierarchy depth and the reference data. Against
  [[documentation-drift]] this is the cleanest repo in the source set.
- **No polish tail.** README, `LICENSE` and `.gitignore` all land in the single final commit
  `91b77f9`; there are no badges and no separate screenshot commit. A **counter-example** to
  [[presentation-polish-tail-commits]], while the README itself is still a
  [[readme-as-guided-tour]].
- **`.gitignore` excludes credential material** (`*.sso`, `*.p12`, `*.jks`, `tnsnames.ora`,
  `wallet/`) alongside SQL*Plus output. Nothing sensitive is in the tree.
- No `.gitattributes` and no Git LFS: the ER PNG and four assignment PDFs are committed as plain
  blobs.

## Git history

The first 8 commits, `796e52c` → `91b77f9`, all land on **2026-07-25 between 12:16:30 and 12:16:33
+0200** — a three-second window. The messages are a clean logical build order (schema → queries →
PL/SQL → OR lab → docs → assignments → diagram → README). Textbook [[import-finished-work-into-git]];
per the interview these bursts were "just cleaning up local folders" — consolidation, not a release.

The 9th, `e233295` on 2026-08-01, is the only commit outside that window and the only one answering
something found later rather than staged in advance.
